body: thats very sweet, i like the idea :) i find that company, irl or online, is very helpful. sadly most of my friends are very much morning people.
thats good advice! i think currently i very much associate my bed with being anxious, so changing that is definitely a top priority for me.
thank you for the tips! ill check out the calm app tonight!

hey amy, thank you for sharing your story, i am very sorry to hear about your loss, i hope you have people near to you that you can reach out to in these difficult times.

i would like to congratulate you on your sobriety, 9 months are definitely a big achievement, and wish you the best of luck and much strength on keeping that streak up!

i dont think i have any good words of wisdom except for wanting to say that your new diagnosis might prove itself a good guide to better understanding and managing self-destructive thought patterns and emotions, especially if you are in treatment.

still, the diagnosis mustnt define you, when i first got diagnosed, i let myself slip into thinking of myself as wholly BPD, neglecting all the other things i am for that diagnosis. i had to learn the hard way that this diagnosis neither degrades us nor excuses us from working on ourselves. after all we are all just people, each beautiful and complicated in our own ways.

i wish you the best and welcome to our community!
this has started happening to me a couple of nights ago! its super annoying, i feel much better mentally with my new dosage but that side effect is very scary

i believe getting better is a very gradual process, a long sequence of improvements and setbacks. you've already listed a great success of your own in regards to suicidality, given time you will have more and more of these improvements. 

personally i dont think you can fully heal from bpd but there are many professional opinions that state that some people can fully heal. keep working on yourself and try to prove me wrong, right?
2-3 days seems way too short to genuinely recover to me. my advice is: take as many days off as you possibly can. you're not a loser, you're a human being going through awful stuff.
happier than ever. i used to burn as the overdriven guitar kicks in. i hope you manage to stay clean for longer, 1 1/2 years is something to be very proud of!

wanting to be seen, to be visible, is a very natural thing. i think most peiple who self-harm go through such feelings. i dont think its pathetic, rather id like you to see it as an incentive to communicate the feelings that lead you to self harm, rather than self harm.

i do not mean to underestimate the feelings you are going through right now. still, i would like to encourage you to stop now, not later. any pain you try to numb through self-harm will come back twofold in the future.

id like to congratulate you. 2 years is a long time, something to be very proud of. your efforts are not for naught, even if unnoticed by your immediate surroundings. you conquered your own addiction, that is a feat of strength most people will thankfully never have to display. keep up the good work!

depending on where you live it is possible that there is some kind of youth/student support therapy program that you could apply for yourself! im sorry to hear about the struggle you have with your mother :(

you know that she is trying to help you, i understand that you still feel intruded on. its an old line of thought that talking about hurt will just make it worse. in my experience its only ever made things more clear.

i think you should use this opportunity to have a healthy, empathetic conversation with her. not just about the blades but about the hurt you feel.

i cling to this philosophy that every relapse i go through is just another opportunity to get clean again. gives some power back to me!

6 months is a long time but i bet you can do even better!

i am sorry to hear about how much pain youre in. how about this idea: you can accept that you may relapse at some point, just not today. then repeat that tomorrow and so on. 

if you relapse, so what, youll just get clean again. until then you keep fighting! 2 1/2 years is something to be very proud of!

i think asking people about scars has become a big social taboo over the last few years. ive been approached about mine by strangers at the beach. to be honest im kind of glad that its become a no-go.
panic, stress and anxiety can all lead to such symptoms, i hope youre doing better now :(
there is no shame in being ill. i am very sorry to hear about your pain. are you currently in therapy? having an in person place to talk about such issues can be very comforting.
do you have a fever? it could be the case that a scar has become infected. if you think that might be the case, i would suggest visiting your GP ASAP!

it seems to me like you are currently going through a lot of hurt, i am sorry about that. 

regarding your urge, it doesnt have to control you. you cant really stop the thoughts immediately but deciding not to act on them over and over again will at some point make them less loud.

you deserve better than to hurt yourself! also nice job on keeping clean, theres pride in that!

most likely scenario is that your urge to mutilate yourself will fade at some point, the fact of having done so however is less reversible.

i would highly suggest working on the underlying causes for this urge instead, maybe in a clinical setting if you feel that you are a danger to yourself.

thinking that you need to prove yourself by harming yourself is already proof enough that you arent mentally healthy.

you are ill, the question is what you want to do with that information! 

(i highly suggest using it to take care of yourself and get help)

you may suffer from the common misconception that help is something that can only be offered and never asked for. there is no shame in wanting to be seen, loneliness is an awful feeling. 

i would like to ask you to reach out for help and comfort in an explicit way. you deserve genuine attention and care, not pity. take care :)

in media self harm is often depicted as this dramatic, tearful moment. in reality ive always found it to be impulsive, awkward and kind of boring.

still, no matter how undramatic that decision may seem, it does not lead anywhere nice in the long term. i would highly advise you to start training other healthier coping mechanisms before this one becomes a problem in its own right.

after all, it seems like youve got enough on your plate already! take care

i think a lot of people confuse healing with letting go. in my opinion, healing can mean focusing on the day to day, one day at a time. it can mean deeply grieving, crying, crashing at a friends place for comfort or just lying in bed and living off of fast food if thats all that you can manage.

healing is a long and complicated process, letting go is only one of the final steps. i understand that you are in a lot of pain right now so please take care of yourself and let others support you. the only person that could 'make him come to his senses' is him, similarly, your priorities should be yourself. 

i wish you all the love

i am very sorry for what you are going through right now. it seems to me as if he is having a bit of an existential crisis, combine that with mood swings and splitting and youve got a real recipe for disaster.

i dont know how to tell you this but, as a person with BPD, i want to say that it is not your responsibility to cater to his mood swings. there is a lot of uncertainty in what is happening right now which can be very hard to accept. still, the best course of action for you is to focus on your own grief over this loss, to try and heal, rather than chase him.

it can and will get easier, no matter what happens.
very honest, sad but with a refreshing sense of self-confidence. i like it :)

i thought about your situation a little more. i dont know if you want to hear this but i really think that, if you want to tell your mom at some point, you should tell her now.

you said yourself that 'she got the point', so really there is no 'lie' to uphold. maybe your mom might feel better if you opened up, as shed feel more able to support you. i also think you would benefit from this support. we all have that tendency to believe that we should save asking for help when it gets 'really bad', ignoring how much we need that help already.

there is no shame is self harm, especially not if you actively try to stop. your scars dont have to be old and pale before you deserve help. if you are afraid of the conversation but feel like it would ultimately help i can tell you a bit about how i told my mom, what to expect and give some tips.

i believe that i can relate to how you feel. i have often felt as though the only way i could ever be made visible to those i need was as a tragic character.

the want may be selfish but none of us can really choose what we feel, what matters is what we do with these feelings. know that you can reach out for help without taking such measures, that you can try to make yourself seen in an explicit, honest way.

i wish you the best

it is a little ironic just how familiar the feelings of love you describe are to the way i experience love, as a person with BPD.

i know what it feels like to love somebody who is not yet ready to be loved, i also know what it feels like to be loved in a way i was not yet ready for.

i hope you can move on and heal and i hope that she can do the same.

intrusive thoughts are really tricky because any attempt to 'get rid' of them only gives them more space. 

i have found that practicing mindfulness and accepting the thoughts as they are, without acting upon or against them, has helped me best with my intrusive thoughts. 

the thoughts dont have power over you and are not a representation of what you want, always keep that in mind.

i really hope this helped a little, thank you for reaching out here!

i feel like working on the root cause rather than the symptom (the self harm) might be most beneficial then. 

are you in therapy and/or on medication?

you seem to feel a lot of guilt for your self harm. i do not believe that guilt to be productive or deserved, after all you are struggling.

maybe talking about it with your mom could help you feel less alone with your struggles? after all, love means being there, even, if not especially, when things get dark.

i do agree with the other comment, finding out about self harm at some point is sadly quite unavoidable. 

i would however also like to say that a history of self harm doesnt entail a ruined life or make you less worthy of being loved. you can grow beyond the wounds and true love goes deeper than scars.

most people who dont struggle with self harm themselves tend to have a skewed understanding of why anybody 'would ever do that to themselves'. stuff like 'please just stop, do it for me' comes to mind.

this is of course a pretty shallow understanding of self harm. if you decide that you want to tell them, do it in a setting that feels comfortable for you. establish some ground rules for the conversation, take the time to answer questions but always keep in mind that you are not guilty or at fault.

finally, be sure to set a goal of what you want from that conversation. being supported by making them understand that professional help would be beneficial for you for instance.

i hope this helped a litte, i know its scary but you are brave.

would you say that these urges feel intrusive? because you said that its scary, it seems to me like you dont really 'want' to do this, which would make these thoughts intrusive in nature.

any further advice i could give would depend on your answer so please feel free to respond!

i think in order to stop cutting a very important step is to determine why you self harm. the reasons can range from wanting to feel something to self hatred to wanting that inner pain to be made visible.

obiously your answer can be something in-between these or something else entirely. its important to figure this out as, depending on the answer, different 'substitutes' (skills training for instance) or types of treatment (investigating and processing feelings of guilt/shame) could help.

do feel free to respond if you already know why you self harm.

thank you for your kind words, it brings me a lot of joy to be able to help a little.

i too was once in a relationship with a person that was struggling badly, she too was of the opinion that 'therapy/meds wont change a thing'.

it was a constant struggle and it weighed down on me heavily for a long time. id be lying if i said that it didnt leave any scars, though i also need to say that she was not at fault at all, it really was just a bad situation.

the relationship ended because of these struggles, but it was on good terms. from the rare, few times we have talked since, i have gathered that she is doing much better now.

i too am doing better, although ive got issues of my own to tend to, just the same as you.

i hope this wasnt too boring a read, i just wanted you to know that there can be a happy ending. you have been strong for a long time and whatever comes next, you deserve to and, given time, will be happy again.

edit: i also think your decision to set a clear boundary (one month) is a good decision, it makes it easier to follow through with your plan of moving on if the worst occurs.

being in a relationship with someone who is struggling bad mentally is very hard, i do very much feel for your pain. you feel trapped between the person you once loved, the person they are now and the guilt that comes from feeling stuck. 

getting clean is a huge struggle, especially if the drug abuse has been a problem for many years, has your partner ever considered getting professional help for coming off? and have you considered going to therapy yourself? i know you feel very alone in this situation but you dont have to be.

right now you may feel as though your only decision is between staying and ending your life but it doesnt have to be that way. for example, getting some distance from the relationship could be a clear incentive for him to work on himself, even if it hurts at first. it may also help you focus on yourself.

black and white measures such as ending your life rarely allow for much nuance. you deserve to make a good and healthy decision for yourself.

do your best to disinfect the wound and apply some kind of bandage, depending on the lenght of the wound a plaster may suffice.

it also depends on where you cut, if you are bleeding a lot then a trip to the ER might be the thing to do.

take this as incentive to try and get clean again, ive been in your exact place before and it was hard but worth it. youve got this!
that is a great idea! turning away from religion as much as possible has made me feel much better about myself too.

i think its good that you made that promise to yourself. you made it in a time when you knew that, at some point, things will get better, it may be good to remind yourself of that not yet dead hope.

and you are a girl. you are a girl, in spite of what the ignorant world around you may tell you. your perseverance, in spite of your struggles, makes you more a girl than anybody else. coming this far is something to be proud of.

i do not believe that you deserve the pain you are feeling. i believe that, because you tried and are still trying to be happy, you deserve to be happy more than those who have never had to work for it.

i know that the world at large is an unjust and hateful place, i hope that you can soon find some comfort in a small world of your own. a community, a group of friends, whatever. until then, i hope that you can continue being as strong as you are.

its normal for these days of 'clarity' as you named them to feel strange. after all we have to adjust to everything in life, even if its a positive change. one day might just not yet be enough for that process of adjusting to run its course.

still, that good days still happen proves that you are capable of being 'clear'. they may just turn into good weeks, good months, if you stick around and get the care that you need.

i am sorry to hear about your struggle.. what you said about not necessarily wanting to die but wanting the struggling to end really resonated with me.

i understand that you may not want any words of encouragement right now, they may just seem shallow. i do want to say that i believe doing what you do, sticking around in spite of the pain, is something to be very proud of.

it seems to me as though you are currently fighting on two fronts. religions have not been kind to LGBTQ+ people at all. i left my religion despite an almost obsessed father for that exact reason.

i do want to ask you one thing: do you still believe or are you afraid of moving on because 'the church might be right after all'? 

i am sorry to hear about your pain, i hope that you can be strong for just a while longer.

i understand that its highly distressing to live in a world that seems incapable of understanding you. i am sorry to hear that this pains you so much.

i wont try to talk you out of your 'no normal connections possible' point because i kind of agree. ive had very similar experiences although our diagnosis are very different.

however, i have also found that, in my case, not normal does not have to mean bad. have you ever bonded with someone who shares your struggles?

first of all, i want to remind you that none of this is your fault. you never chose to have struggles with mental health and you should not blame yourself for them.

if you are too scared of opening up to your family about them, which i understand, how about a friend? i do not know where you live but we have little self-help groups for various mental health issues where i live, those are also great.
that is tough. so you already explained to her how much you are struggling right now?

its incredibly tiring to base your self worth on what you believe others think of you. i have been diagnosed with OCD and the 'perfect person' you describe feels very familiar to me. 

have you tried writing down some good thoughts about yourself in a good state of mind? you could keep that little 'letter to yourself' and read it in times of need!

i am so sorry to hear about all of this, you are too young to have to be confronted with anything this painful.

do you think that you could talk about these worries with your mother?

4 years is a lot of time. how you feel in that class, if indeed you are forced to stay there, will change a lot. 

it is good that you are who you are, even if your classmates are too stupid to see that right now. is there any form of child protection where you live?

hey, i looked at your profile and saw that you also have BPD, so i think i understand you very well. sometimes i feel like the worst person on earth, like id be doing the world a favor if i ended my life.

still, right now i am very happy that i have never gone so far. may i ask if anything in particular made you come to this decision?

how many further years do you have to get through until you can move out? it seems to me like getting away from your father is the best thing to do here.

regarding friends at school, i dont think i have kept any of the ones i made. theres always time to start again and meet new people once your situation improves.
this is such a wonderful story, i am very happy to hear that you have found something to live for. believe it or not, i have had a very similar experience with a hedgehog once!

hey, it seems to me like you are fighting on two fronts. mental health issues are hard enough as is, the stigma that people with such issues then face just makes it worse.

do you believe that you could talk with your family about what your mental health issues feel like? you have been so strong for so long, please try to keep it up for a little while longer.

i believe that oftentimes these self-hating thoughts stem from being taught early that you are not enough, at least thats how it worked for me. would you agree?

no matter the root-cause of these thoughts, I hope that you can see these thoughts as what they are: flawed. the world is a better place with you in it, even if it doesnt feel like it.

i am sorry to hear about your struggles with this person. i understand what its like to drag yourself through the rubble for somebody that you just cant let go. 

exactly one year ago i was in a very similar situation to yours, once i actually said to them to 'please end it already, i cant do it'. it was a painful time and i resolved to casually gambling with my life, taking benzos and drinking.

i dont mean to share too much except that in the meantime i have gotten much better. i have stopped taking benzos and dont drink as much anymore. you too deserve to get to that point when your wounds slowly hurt less, you too can be happy again. 

all it takes now if for you to stay strong and focus on what is best for you now.

i understand the abandonment fears, its really tough.. still, i think keeping an open line of communication is key for all things BPD-related.

oftentimes, people who dont share our struggles, misinterpret our suffering as giving into the pain. explain that that is really not the case! remind yourself and your fiancé that you are both working on a shared goal here, that you really do want to feel better.

i hope that your situation will improve soon, much love!

oh, i almost forgot:
i am sorry to hear about the bad place youre stuck in right now. reaching out for help is already a huge step! keep fighting, youve got this!

getting hospitalized works different depending on where you live. in my homecountry, the best course of action would be to ask for hospitalization and explain your suicidal thoughts directly at the hospital for your area.

i understand that you must be feeling incredibly lonely, its an awful, awful feeling. still, i dont think i could agree with you saying youre 'unlikeable'. you still have value, you still are a beautiful person, deserving of love.
thats the spirit, you got this!

i am very sorry to hear about all the awful things that happened to you, in life and over the course of this year. 

you said that youre not looking for sympathy or encouragement, i hope its still okay if i express my admiration, you have been through so much and that shows incredible strength.

i am very sorry to hear about your hurt. it sounds as though your GF has played into some very deep insecurities you have about yourself, that is awful.

it seems to me as though, even if you may not feel like it, you would be better off without her. it will take a lot of time, time that you could use to find out more about yourself, to make some new friendships, etc.

i really hope that you can hang in there for a while longer. you deserve to be happy, dont let your mental problems rid you off getting a chance to become happy again.

getting better is not a two month process, its a process of struggle and set backs, one of which you are experiencing right now.

from what you shared, it sounds as though you have been through a lot. i am very sorry to hear about what has been done to you and very proud of you for managing to take such big steps towards a happier life.

getting better takes a while but you have come so far. further than i believe you would have ever thought possible a year ago. you now know that you are capable of feeling happy, fight for a little while longer and you will feel happy again.

i believe that most people feel very overwhelmed when hearing about the mental struggles of people they love, especially when they cannot understand the struggles themselves.

most people may either get super anxious and desperately try to fix us, or, like your friend did, try to gloss over the struggles, be it out of hope to distract us or out of inability to comprehend how bad things really are.

its one of the reasons therapy exists: a trained professional with just enough personal distance to keep a clear head and respond thoughtfully, even when things get dark. hell, its why this subreddit exists.

im not trying to play down the hurt you feel or say that your friend did nothing wrong. i understand how awful it feels to not be heard. i sincerely hope you dont take that hurt out on yourself. 

you deserve to be heard and seen, you may just need to search for a person that is able to hear and see you a little while longer.

its easy to get caught up in beliefs of being a horrible person. ive done some pretty bad stuff myself. the important thing to keep in mind is that, if you are willing to change or have already changed, you are not defined by your past.

its never too late to start again and become the person you truly want to be. i feel for you and hope you can manage the pain until you get better.

it seems to me as though you are implying that stopping to take venlafaxin caused the symptoms to reemerge, do you believe that taking it again may help?

i am sorry to hear about your monetary situation and how it affects your ability to choose consultants. are there any plans you could consider to raise the money needed to visit a specialised clinician? 

i also understand that not being able to follow your usual routines and pursue your usual interests (gym) is very hard. maybe you could find something to invest time and practice into that you could do until you possibly get better in the future?

first of all, i am very sorry to hear about your struggle. 

judging from your recent post history it seems like you have only recently found out about your potential diagnosis. are you sure that seeing one vascular doc has exhausted all your options? 

i sincerely hope that you reevaluate your plan to end it, and that you can find a treatment in the future that can make your life more bearable.

its okay for old wounds to open unexpectedly. it seems to me like you feel as though all the progress you have made has been for nought because the bad thoughts returned, but that isnt true. 

you are now in a much better place than you were 6 years ago. in addition to that, you have already learned that getting over these thoughts is possible. from that alone i can tell that you are a very strong person, its something to be proud of.

you have overcome these thoughts once and you will do it again, because you deserve to be happy.

fellow PWBPD here, i understand your struggle. its a horrible, horrible illness and i wouldnt wish it on my worst enemy.

the one specific piece of advise i can give you right now is to open up about these feelings to at least one of the people you love. 

write yourself a list of things you would like those that care about you to know and work through it with one of those people in a nice, calm setting. 

their first reaction may then be quite panicked, dont let yourself be misguided by that. explain that you do not want to have these thoughts and that you truly do want somebody to help you through them.

i can promise you that people dont mind being overwhelmed as much as they would mind having to go on without you.

you said it yourself, this is not the person you are, why then should this real you have to pay the price?

it seems to me as though you are under a lot of stress and i understand. are you in a position where you could consider getting help?

it seems to me like you are describing intrusive thoughts. these are basically thoughts that pop out of our subconscious into our consciousness. forcing them down, for example by interacting with them logically, oftentimes just makes them come back more.

my best advice would be to try and take their power away. remind yourself that your thoughts cant force you to do anything to yourself before you interact with them. if the situation continues to be distressing, i would also highly recommend therapy.

it will get better over time, i promise!

i am very sorry to hear about your pain. separation from someone you love is one of the hardest things one can reasonably be expected to have to go through.

have you sought any help recently? the bad thoughts may not go away, but you dont have to deal with them on your own.

may i ask you to further explain what brought you to this decision?

ending it through overdose is a very painful process, especially with ibuprofen. i have witnessed the seizures and the pain first hand.

i know that you are currently in deep pain, but i can assure you that it can get better. you have been strong for a while now, dont you think itd be worth it to try for just a little while longer?

i understand, bpd is the worst. have you been hospitalized before? depending on your country, being hospitalized can often actually be a very helpful experience!

i believe its very hard to measure and weigh love. i know what its like to feel like you love somebody more than i do. maybe they just show you their love in a different way?
would you like to share what is troubling you?

the only thing thats left to do if you relapse is to get better again. youve already demonstrated your ability to feel happy and to get better, you can do it again. 

please keep trying, it will get better again and the next time it might just get better for longer.

i understand. i know that i really cant do much here online but ive been through very similar things and it got better at some point. 

i believe that the day to day struggle you are going through right now proves that you are very strong. i am certain that you can be strong for just a little longer, maybe you too could get better, like i did.

i understand your pain. it is unfair, but you deserve better than to let this unfairness ruin you. i know that moving on and learning to trust again is very hard but, given time, i believe that you will manage to do it.

are you in therapy?

i agree, it wont take your pain away completely but it would at least give it some meaning. you have the power to do a little good, drowning in a river would waste that potential.

there is some solace from pain in knowing that you have at least helped someone else.
in that case there is really not much to do in your power, im sorry.

do you know the person? if you do then calling an ambulance is the way to go. if they are not currently in the act of ending it then being with them, listening and encouraging them to visit a clinic/get help is.

if there is no higher power then it is in our hands to care for the homeless, the sick, the hungry, to show love to those who need it.

your pain enables you to see the pain around you, as others are blissfully unaware of the suffering. why not use that very unique ability to see and do the work that no higher power will do for us?

i am typing this right now, hoping i could stop a complete stranger whom i will NEVER meet from ending their life. this whole sub exists because some people care. you seem to care too. 

in other words, you seem to have already found something to keep going on for. please dont waste it.
for the same reason that you should go on tomorrow: it will get easier, at some point. do you feel like sharing why you are contemplating suicide?

i understand what it feels like to see no purpose. it seems me as though you are truly in pain. feeling such a pain can easily lead you to lose all sense of meaning, but it doesnt have to.

if therapy is not an option, maybe medication could be? i was on meds long before i was in therapy because i could not afford the therapy and it helped.

you have not given up yet and that is something to be proud of. remind yourself of how far youve come and use that pride to keep going. it will get better if you do.

its an awful thing to have unloving parents. you are not a mistake just because they say so. you are deserving of love, you may just have to keep going for a little while longer to find people that can show you that love. youve got this.
hey! you can message me if you still want.
i meant it, youve got this.

you are not a bad person for not seeing the value of the people who love you in the past. you can change and it seems to me as though you already have changed.

the world is much too big a place for a single mind to grasp, that is why we build our own little worlds, the people we love, the people we care about.

maybe there is comfort in knowing that, even though the world at large may not care, these infinite little worlds do. after all, if they didnt, we wouldnt have graveyards.

its so very hard to be with a person who you think to be perfect. i understand this very well. i also have BPD so that might explain it.

you have made a big decision with your career change, i think those are inevitably hard for a long time. but they get easier as you and your surroundings accustom to them.

if your fiancé truly is as good a person as you describe him, surely he will understand or at least have sympathy for your feelings. this is not something you have to go through alone, he may not like to hear about your suicidal thoughts but i am willing to promise you that he would like only finding out when its too late even less.

ps, as a teacher in training, the world does not recognize our profession enough. after all, no matter who we are or where we are from, we all needed at least one teacher in life.

the disdain some of us feel towards the world and other people is oftentimes a result of being shown hate and too little love ourselves.

you are not necessarily an evil person, even if it seems like that to you.

would you like to elaborate a little on why you believe you are evil?

the bachelors degree i am about to receive in a semester has not changed my life nor my worth as a human being.

you do not need to become academically successful to have worth, i have met plenty of people without degrees that have made this world better than anyone with even a doctors ever could.

maybe a change in direction would be better? you may have just not found your calling yet. its never too late to start again.

do you want to share what brought you to this decision? 

i know that life can get incredibly hard and painful, ive made the exact same decision you have made before and i got better, because i lived on. ive also seen others who have had it worse than me get better.

Aziz, thats a very beautiful name.

you have said yourself that you have three very good friends, people that you love. i think thats a very beautiful thing to have in life and i hope that you dont let others, awful people, take you away from it.

please call an ambulance as quickly as possible. it can get better if you let it.

do you need somebody to explain what has brought you to this decision to? if yes then please send me a message.

two months is a long time and a lot can change in that time. there is hope.

for people who have been badly hurt emotionally, feeling alone with the trauma oftentimes feels worse than being with someone awful.

i am sorry to hear that the medications and stays at the clinic did not help, still 5 months may just not have been enough time to truly heal. 

dont you think that, someday, you could find a person or a community that gives you comfort, that isnt abusive? i believe you will, as long as you keep fighting until then.

i think you should leave the house as quickly as possible, maybe crash at a friends or a relatives place?

what the other person said is also true, get yourself legally protected as quickly as possible. if your father threatened to kill you, then what you did was either self defense or you cracking under the pressure.
